newsitem.title: USA: Dakotah says sees Q4 sales up 40 percent.
newsitem.headline: Dakotah says sees Q4 sales up 40 percent.

text.p: Dakotah Inc said Wednesday it expects fourth quarter sales of about $15 million, a 40 percent rise from last year's fourth quarter.
The expectation is based on the current level of open orders, chief executive officer Troy Jones Jr. said in the bedding maker's third quarter statement.
Shipments will begin in the 1997 first quarter of a new line of throws, pillows and bed coverings featuring Walt Disney Co characters, the company said.
Third-quarter earnings of $0.10 versus $0.05 a year ago would have been higher if not for an operating loss in July, Dakotah said.

Dakotah makes home furnishings products from Polarfleece, a fabric produced by Malden Mills. While Polarfleece products helped third quarter sales, earnings were hurt by inadequate deliveries of the fabric and by initial production costs at its Polarfleece products plant in Redfield, S.D., the company said.
Revenues rose 53 percent to $12.6 million due mainly to the Polarfleece line and expanded sales of pillows, table linen, bedding and accessories, it said.

But gross margins were hurt by the manufacturing start-up, insufficient fabric deliveries mainly in July and August, and increasing sales of products with high raw materials content, and declined to 24.6 percent from 27.7 percent in the 1995 third quarter, Dakotah said.

"Dakotah's sales strength in this difficult retailing environment is a testament to the reception our products have received at the retail level," chief executive officer Troy James Jr. said in the statement.
